public_rationale: Environmental burdens and risks are documented. There is also credible evidence that electricity-demand projections contain duplication and upward bias. The missing link is proof that the relevant data centers were being built beyond substantiated demand. Low vacancy and substantial preleasing caution against that inference, although neither proves long-term utilization. The compound claim is therefore unresolved.
limitations: The environmental and demand studies do not cover identical facilities or workloads.
The demand-bias report was commissioned by the Southern Environmental Law Center; CBRE operates in the property industry.
Environmental risks can exist even when construction meets real demand.

our_interpretation: Environmental threat means material risks from emissions, water consumption, or other resource burdens attributable to generative-AI infrastructure.
Too much speculation means construction materially exceeds demand supported by credible usage, commitments, and reasonable projections. Uncertainty alone is insufficient.
I assess construction and risks existing by February 23, 2026. Announced projects, connection requests, completed buildings, and utilized computing capacity are distinct.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence links generative-AI data-center construction to material environmental risks and shows that the relevant construction exceeds substantiated demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence demonstrates no material environmental threat from the relevant buildout, or establishes that the allegedly excessive construction is justified by credible demand.

The analysis identifies duplicated connection requests and demand projections inconsistent with chip-supply constraints. This supports concern about speculative planning, but excess requests are not proof that excess data centers were actually built.

evidence.explanation: CBRE reports 1.6% primary-market vacancy and 74.3% preleasing of construction capacity, tempering a broad overbuilding inference. Its coverage combines cloud and AI demand, and leases do not establish actual computing utilization or future profitability.
